hmca-2027.about:
Harvard Model Congress Asia (HMCA) is organised by Harvard College students and is the Asian edition of Harvard Model Congress. HMCA 2027 takes place on 11–13 January 2027 at the University of Seoul. Delegates role-play members of the US Congress, the executive and the courts, and international bodies, writing and debating legislation and resolutions in committees led by Harvard staff.

It is designed for high-school students from around the world; schools register delegations and students can also register independently. Conference guides, committee information and a scholarship application are published on the official site.

A strong choice for students interested in government, law and policy who want a Harvard-run simulation without travelling to the US.
highlights: Independent and school-delegation registration; scholarships available
hmca-2027.eligibility: High-school students worldwide, registering through their school or as independent delegates. English is the working language.
how_to_apply: Read Registration Information on hmcasia.org
Fill in the school or independent delegate registration form
Pay through the payment portal
Receive committee assignments and prepare with the delegate guide
hmca-2027.costs: Independent delegate fee USD 415; school fee USD 200 plus USD 375 per school delegate (official payment portal). Travel and hotel extra; scholarships available.

hosa-international-leadership-conference.about:
HOSA members compete in dozens of events in health science knowledge, health professions skills, emergency preparedness, leadership and teamwork. Students first compete at their chartered association's conference (US states and international associations) in early 2027; top finishers advance to the ILC.

The ILC also includes general sessions, workshops and a research forum, and draws thousands of students interested in medicine, nursing and public health.
hosa-international-leadership-conference.eligibility: Secondary and post-secondary students who are members of a HOSA chapter (US states and international chartered associations).
how_to_apply: Join or start a HOSA chapter at your school
Choose your competitive event(s)
Compete at your chartered-association conference
Qualify for the ILC in June 2027
hosa-international-leadership-conference.costs: HOSA membership dues, conference registration and travel (paid by students/schools).

hoya-hacks-2027.about:
Hoya Hacks 2027 is Georgetown University's hackathon in Washington, D.C.. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at Georgetown University in Washington, D.C. from 2027-01-22 to 2027-01-24. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.
highlights: Build a portfolio project in one weekend
hoya-hacks-2027.eligibility: Students enrolled at a college or university (many MLH events also admit high-school students aged 18+, and some all ages 13+ with consent). Participants must follow the MLH Code of Conduct. International students may attend but must arrange their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open https://www.hoyahacks.com/ and sign up for application updates or apply if the form is open
Form a small team or join one at the event
Complete the application and accept the MLH Code of Conduct
Confirm your spot when accepted and arrange your own travel unless reimbursement is offered
Attend in person and submit your project for judging
hoya-hacks-2027.costs: Free to attend; meals, snacks and workspace provided. Travel and accommodation are usually at your own cost unless the event announces travel reimbursement.

hpair-virtual-harvard-youth-leadership-s.about:
The Harvard Youth Leadership Summit (HYLS) is organised by HPAIR, a student-run organisation at Harvard College. The virtual 2026 edition takes place online on 18-20 December 2026.

It is aimed at ambitious secondary-school students who want to engage with global issues and prepare for university. The programme includes college panels in which Harvard students share their journeys from high school to college, mentorship, research and guidance sessions, and talks by invited speakers.

Applications are via the form on the HPAIR website by 20 November 2026; a delegate fee may apply (shown during application).
highlights: College panels and mentorship for high-schoolers
hpair-virtual-harvard-youth-leadership-s.eligibility: Secondary-school students from any country with good English.
how_to_apply: Read the HYLS page on hpair.org.
Complete the online application form.
Submit by 20 November 2026.
Pay any delegate fee if accepted and join online.
hpair-virtual-harvard-youth-leadership-s.costs: A delegate fee may apply; check the application form. Online, so no travel costs.

hscmun-iii-2027.about:
HSCMUN is an academically rigorous one-day Model UN at Hillfield Strathallan College in Hamilton, Ontario. Delegates who want to be eligible for awards submit a position paper.

The conference runs 20 February 2027 at Hillfield Strathallan College, Hamilton, Canada. It is open to high school students (school delegations or independent delegates). Working language: English.

Use the 'School Delegation Registration' or 'Independent Registration' forms on the official page. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
hscmun-iii-2027.eligibility: Open to high school students (school delegations or independent delegates). Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Use the 'School Delegation Registration' or 'Independent Registration' forms on the official page.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
hscmun-iii-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

iaeste-internship-exchange-2027.about:
IAESTE is a worldwide student-exchange association, founded in 1948, that swaps paid, career-focused internships between national committees. Employers in member countries offer placements, and each national committee nominates its own students for offers abroad. All internships are paid (examples on the platform: 2,350 EUR/month in Austria, 2,300 CHF/month in Switzerland, 15,000 KES/month in Kenya), and committees help with housing and visas.

Students register on the IAESTE Exchange Platform and contact their national or local committee, which sets eligibility and the selection timeline. Once selected and nominated, documents go to the employer for acceptance. Current listings show application deadlines between 6 November 2026 and 28 March 2027.
iaeste-internship-exchange-2027.eligibility: University students in technical and scientific fields from IAESTE member or cooperating countries; criteria set by each national committee (check iaeste.org/countries).
how_to_apply: Check that your country has an IAESTE committee (iaeste.org/countries)
Register on the IAESTE Exchange Platform
Contact your national/local committee and pass its selection
Get nominated for an offer and accepted by the employer
iaeste-internship-exchange-2027.costs: Internships are paid (stipend set per offer); travel usually paid by the student.

IASMUN is the second edition of the Model UN conference hosted by the International American School in Warsaw.

The conference runs 20–22 November 2026 at the International American School, Warsaw, Poland. It is open to secondary school students and school delegations. Working language: English.

icpc-online-challenge-2026-huawei.about:
The ICPC Online Challenge is a heuristic ('marathon') contest: instead of exact answers, participants submit programs whose scores improve as their solutions get better, over a two-week window. Previous editions have been powered by Huawei with problems from its research labs, and top performers win prizes and recognition from ICPC.

It is open to registered Codeforces users, making it an accessible way for university and advanced high-school programmers to gain ICPC-branded results.
highlights: Free, online, open to Codeforces users
icpc-online-challenge-2026-huawei.eligibility: Anyone with a Codeforces account can take part; prize eligibility is set in the contest announcement (check age/country rules).
how_to_apply: Create a Codeforces account
Register for the contest on the Codeforces contests page
Read the problem when it opens on 5 Nov 2026
Submit improving solutions until the window closes

if-design-student-award-2027.about:
The iF DESIGN STUDENT AWARD invites students of all design disciplines (product, communication, interior, architecture, service design and more) to submit concepts addressing social and environmental challenges framed by the SDGs. Over 7,000 concepts were submitted in 2026; 90 were honoured from 22 countries.

Entries are judged online in March 2027 and by a final jury in Berlin on 23 April 2027 on problem-solving, impact, innovation and aesthetics. Winners gain international recognition and a share of EUR 50,000.
if-design-student-award-2027.eligibility: Design students and recent graduates worldwide (see iF rules for graduation-date limits).
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 rules and SDG briefs on ifdesign.com
Develop your design concept
Register and submit online by 3 Feb 2027
if-design-student-award-2027.costs: Check the iF site for fees; the student award has historically been free to enter.

iihf-world-championship-2027-volunteers.about:
Germany hosts the IIHF Ice Hockey World Championship from 14 to 30 May 2027 in Düsseldorf and Mannheim (with one game in Gelsenkirchen). The organising committee is recruiting volunteers for roles such as hospitality, transport, accreditation and fan services, both in the lead-up to and during the tournament, with structured orientation and training before your first shift.

Volunteers must be 18 by 1 May 2027, have a smartphone and email, and be available for at least 7 days (longer availability is preferred). You can list three preferred work areas. Applicants from abroad are expressly welcome, but very good German is mandatory (English is a plus).

Benefits include meals on volunteer days, volunteer clothing you keep, a volunteer certificate, access to the Home of Volunteers lounge and at least one game ticket. It is a strong CV line for students interested in sport management, events or tourism.
highlights: World's largest annual winter sports event, Düsseldorf and Mannheim, 14–30 May 2027
Meals, uniform, certificate and at least one game ticket
iihf-world-championship-2027-volunteers.eligibility: Aged 18+ by 1 May 2027; available for at least 7 days; very good German required, English an advantage; valid email address and smartphone; must attend the kick-off meeting and training. Non-residents of Germany may apply but must arrange their own travel, lodging and accident insurance.
how_to_apply: Read the volunteer overview and both FAQs on iihf.com.
Create an account on the official volunteer platform (iihf.eventvolunteers.de).
Choose your city (Düsseldorf and/or Mannheim), availability and three preferred work areas.
Wait for the selection decision (expected by the end of 2026), then attend kick-off and training.
iihf-world-championship-2027-volunteers.costs: Free. Meals during shifts, volunteer clothing, a certificate and at least one game ticket are provided. Travel, lodging and accident insurance are the volunteer's responsibility.

ilmunc-india-3-2027.about:
ILMUNC India is the Indian edition of the Ivy League Model United Nations Conference, organised by undergraduates from the University of Pennsylvania, who also run ILMUNC in Philadelphia and editions in Dubai, China, Vietnam and Peru. ILMUNC India 3.0 takes place on 8–10 January 2027 at Chitkara University, Chandigarh region.

The programme opens with a keynote, then runs general, specialised and crisis committees chaired by Penn staff, with social events such as Delegate Fest. Assistant Director (staff) applications are also offered.

A chance for Indian high-school students to experience an Ivy League-run conference at home.
highlights: Run by University of Pennsylvania students
Social events and AD staff roles
ilmunc-india-3-2027.eligibility: High-school students in India and the region, as school delegations or individuals. English is the working language.

ilmunc-vietnam-2027.about:
ILMUNC Vietnam brings the University of Pennsylvania's Ivy League Model United Nations Conference to Southeast Asia. The 2027 edition runs on 12–14 March 2027 in Ho Chi Minh City.

Committees include UNESCO, DISEC, SPECPOL, a historical 1956 UN General Assembly emergency session and a crisis committee on the Deepwater Horizon board of commissioners; background guides and the agenda are published on the site.

Good for high-school students in Vietnam and neighbouring countries who want US-university-run committees close to home.

imc-university-mathematics-2027.about:
The IMC is the main international olympiad for university mathematics students, run since 1994 and traditionally hosted at the American University in Bulgaria, Blagoevgrad. Around 600 students from 200+ universities take part, usually as university teams with a team leader, though individuals may also register.

The competition has two days of problems; medals and honourable mentions are awarded. Check the IMC site for the 2027 venue confirmation, fees (registration covers accommodation and meals) and registration window.
imc-university-mathematics-2027.eligibility: Undergraduate students (up to age ~23, per IMC rules) at any university worldwide; usually entered by their university's team leader.
how_to_apply: Ask your mathematics department whether it sends a team
Watch the IMC 2027 registration page for the opening date
Register through your team leader (or individually)
Pay the participation fee and arrange travel/visa
imc-university-mathematics-2027.costs: Participation fee covers accommodation and meals during the competition (amount published at registration); travel is self-funded or paid by universities.

imperial-global-summer-school-2027.about:
Imperial's Global Summer School is a two-week residential pre-university programme in London for academically strong 16- and 17-year-olds from around the world. In week one students follow a subject stream (Chemistry, Data Science & AI, Engineering, Medicine & Life Sciences or Physics) with lectures, labs and workshops; in week two they join mixed teams for an Innovation Challenge run by the Imperial Enterprise Lab. Students live in Imperial's Prince's Gardens halls and get guidance on applying to UK universities.

Places are given on a rolling, first-come basis and popular subjects fill months ahead, so apply as soon as the 2027 window opens. Imperial offers no scholarships or bursaries for this programme.
highlights: Subject week in chemistry, data science & AI, engineering, medicine or physics
Innovation Challenge with the Imperial Enterprise Lab
Live on campus in South Kensington; UK university application advice
imperial-global-summer-school-2027.eligibility: Aged 16 by the start and not 18 before or during the programme; mostly A*/A (9–7) at GCSE or international equivalent with at least A in maths and relevant sciences; strong English. All nationalities.

Apply online as early as possible (rolling admission)
Pay the full fee within 14 days of an unconditional offer (7 days later in the cycle)
imperial-global-summer-school-2027.costs: 2026 fee GBP 7,695, for the residential programme (tuition and on-campus accommodation; see the fees page for exactly what is included); flights and visa extra. No scholarships, discounts or bursaries.

imun3-una-boulder-2027.about:
IMUN3 is UNA Boulder's third inter-generational Model UN: a single-morning simulation of negotiations on 'The Black Sea Grain Framework', with about 80 seats shared by students and adults. Breakfast and lunch are provided.

The conference runs 23 January 2027 at Academy Mapleton Hill, Grand Hall, Boulder, United States. It is open to students and adults of all ages (inter-generational; 80 seats). Working language: English.

Sign up via the registration form linked from the UNA Boulder announcement; seats are limited to about 80. Breakfast and lunch are provided; see the UNA Boulder page for any participation fee. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.

imun3-una-boulder-2027.eligibility: Open to students and adults of all ages (inter-generational; 80 seats). Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.

Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
imun3-una-boulder-2027.costs: Breakfast and lunch are provided; see the UNA Boulder page for any participation fee. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

imuna-2027.about:
IMUNA is a long-running Dutch school conference — 2027 is its 33rd (XXXIII) edition — held at the Murmellius Gymnasium in Alkmaar. The 2027 executive staff has been appointed.

The conference runs 4–6 June 2027 at Murmellius Gymnasium, Alkmaar, Netherlands. It is open to secondary school students in school delegations. Working language: English.

School registration opens on the official site (see the 'Participate' section and news updates). The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. imunbp-2026.about:
IMUNBP is the international Model UN of the BetàniaPatmos school in Barcelona, with committees, a GA, host-family options and insurance information for visiting schools.

The conference runs 9–13 December 2026 at Escola BetàniaPatmos, Barcelona, Spain. It is open to secondary school students and school delegations. Working language: English.

Schools register via the 'Registration' page; fees, insurance and host-family details are on the official site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Host-family accommodation can be requested. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.

indian-computing-olympiad-2027.about:
The ICO first round has two parts: ZIO, a written problem-solving exam at centres across India, and ZCO, a programming exam. Qualifiers from either sit INOI (the national olympiad, C++), and the top students attend the IOI Training Camp, which selects India's team for IOI 2027 in Germany.

There is no lower age limit; students must still be in school (Class 12 or below).
highlights: Two entry routes: written ZIO or programming ZCO
indian-computing-olympiad-2027.eligibility: Students registered in school up to Class 12 in India (any board), no lower age limit.
how_to_apply: Register for ZIO/ZCO on the IARCS site
Practise with past ZIO/ZCO papers
Sit ZIO on 21 Nov 2026 and/or ZCO on 12 Dec 2026
Qualify for INOI in early 2027
indian-computing-olympiad-2027.costs: Registration fee per exam (see IARCS announcement).

informatik-biber-2026.about:
The Informatik-Biber is the entry point to Germany's family of computing competitions run by BWINF: short interactive tasks on algorithms, logic and data, no programming required. Teachers register their school and run the test in class during the Biber weeks.

Interested students can continue with the Jugendwettbewerb Informatik (from spring, for beginners in programming) and the Bundeswettbewerb Informatik, which leads to IOI selection.
highlights: Free, in class, no coding needed
Gateway to Germany's informatics olympiad track
informatik-biber-2026.eligibility: Students in grades 3–13 at schools in Germany (and German schools abroad), registered by a teacher.
how_to_apply: Ask a teacher to register the school on bwinf.de
Try past Biber tasks
Take the test in class during 9–20 Nov 2026

informatik-biber-switzerland-2026.about:
The Swiss Informatik-Biber (Castor in French, Castoro in Italian) offers age-appropriate interactive tasks on algorithms and logic for all school levels, in German, French and Italian. Teachers act as coordinators and run the contest in class during the window.

Top participants are invited to the Biber final, and interested students can move on to the Swiss Olympiad in Informatics.
informatik-biber-switzerland-2026.eligibility: School students in Switzerland and Liechtenstein, registered by a teacher-coordinator.
how_to_apply: Teacher registers on informatik-biber.ch
Practise with past tasks
Take the contest in class 9–20 Nov 2026

innovateher-2027.about:
InnovateHer 2027 is Purdue's hackathon for women and gender minorities in tech. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at Purdue University in West Lafayette from 2027-02-06 to 2027-02-07. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.
highlights: Build a portfolio project in one weekend

Complete the application and accept the MLH Code of Conduct
Confirm your spot when accepted and arrange your own travel unless reimbursement is offered
Attend in person and submit your project for judging
innovateher-2027.costs: Free to attend; meals, snacks and workspace provided. Travel and accommodation are usually at your own cost unless the event announces travel reimbursement.

international-childrens-peace-prize-2027.about:
The International Children's Peace Prize is awarded each year by the KidsRights Foundation to a child who stands up for children's rights. Past winners include Malala Yousafzai and Greta Thunberg; the story of the 2025 winner reached an estimated 1.5 billion people.

Nominees must be under 18 and have made a real difference for children's rights; an expert committee of international children's-rights experts chooses the winner. The winner's cause is supported through the KidsRights fund and the Desmond Tutu Study and Care Fund.

Anyone can nominate a child via the KidsRights website when nominations are open; check the prize page for the 2027 criteria and dates.
highlights: Global stage for a young children's-rights activist
Winners chosen by an international expert committee
Support for the winner's cause and education
international-childrens-peace-prize-2027.eligibility: Children under 18, from any country, who actively stand up for children's rights. Nominations are made by others (organisations, teachers, family).
how_to_apply: Read the nomination criteria on the KidsRights prize page.
Gather evidence of the child's work and impact.
Submit the nomination form when nominations open.
Shortlisted nominees are reviewed by the Expert Committee.

international-history-olympiad-2027.about:
The International History Olympiad, organised by International Academic Competitions, brings together top young history students for quiz-bowl style team and individual events, history-themed games, and excursions. Students qualify through regional History Bee and History Bowl tournaments held in Asia, Canada, Europe and the US during the school year, or by taking the online Olympiad Qualifying Exam.

IAC also runs online practice tournaments, so students in countries without regional events can still prepare and qualify.
highlights: Week of history competitions in Berlin
Qualify via regional tournaments or exam
international-history-olympiad-2027.eligibility: Primary and secondary students who qualify through IAC History Bee/Bowl regionals or the Olympiad Qualifying Exam.
how_to_apply: Register for a History Bee/Bowl regional tournament or the qualifying exam on iacompetitions.com
Qualify during the 2026–27 season
Register for the Olympiad and pay the participation fee
Travel to Berlin for 17–24 Jul 2027
international-history-olympiad-2027.costs: Tournament and Olympiad fees plus travel (see the Costs page on historyolympiad.com).

international-model-parliament-paris-202.about:
International Model Parliament is a Paris debating conference simulating parliaments and a Model Congress rather than only UN bodies.

The conference runs 22–25 April 2027 at venues in Paris, France. It is open to high school and university students. Working language: English.

Chair applications opened on 30 Oct 2026; delegate applications open in December 2026 via the registration link on the official site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.

isep-exchange-fall-2027.about:
ISEP is a non-profit network of universities in more than 50 countries. In ISEP Exchange you swap places with a student from another member institution: you pay tuition and fees to your home university (and usually housing and meals there, depending on the programme) and study abroad for a semester or year. You can list up to 10 universities and ISEP places you based on exchange space and your academic needs.

ISEP Direct is a separate, fee-based route where you pick a destination and pay a set fee that includes tuition, insurance and usually housing. To use ISEP your home university must be a member (check the member directory). Exchange applications for Semester 1 or full-year programmes starting July-October 2027 are due before 1 March 2027; priority deadlines are earlier.
highlights: Choose up to 10 universities in 50+ countries
isep-exchange-fall-2027.eligibility: Students enrolled at an ISEP member institution (check the member directory); requirements set by the home ISEP coordinator.
how_to_apply: Check that your university is an ISEP member
Meet your ISEP coordinator
Choose up to 10 Exchange sites on search.isepstudyabroad.org
Submit the ISEP application before 1 March 2027 (or the priority deadline)
Receive placement and apply for visa
isep-exchange-fall-2027.costs: Exchange: home-institution tuition and fees; ISEP application fee and personal costs. Direct: fixed programme fee.

itu-academy-free-online-courses.about:
ITU Academy is the training platform of the International Telecommunication Union, the UN specialised agency for information and communication technologies. It lists many courses that are free, both self-paced and instructor-led, on topics such as artificial intelligence (technical, business and regulatory aspects), cybersecurity, GovStack digital government building blocks, wireless infrastructure, spectrum management and digital inclusion.

Instructor-led online courses run on fixed dates (for example a free course on the technical, business and regulatory aspects of AI runs 30 November – 7 December 2026); self-paced courses can be started at any time. Successful participants receive ITU certificates.

Courses are aimed at students, professionals and policymakers; registration is via a free ITU Academy account, and some courses have limited seats.
highlights: AI, cybersecurity, digital government and connectivity
itu-academy-free-online-courses.eligibility: Anyone; some instructor-led courses target professionals or have limited places. Mostly in English, some in French, Spanish, Arabic and other UN languages.
how_to_apply: Create a free ITU Academy account.
Filter the catalogue for 'Free' courses.
Enrol in a self-paced course or register for an instructor-led one before it starts.
Complete assessments to earn the certificate.
itu-academy-free-online-courses.costs: Many courses free; some ITU courses are paid (filter by price).

ja-europe-gen-e-2027-luxembourg.about:
Gen-E is JA Europe's annual entrepreneurship festival, bringing together the best student companies and start-ups from across Europe. It is the final stage of the JA Company Programme (secondary school) and Start Up Programme (higher education), in which teams create and run a real mini-company during the school year.

The road has four stages: running your company in school (September–May), the year-round Virtual Gen-E online expo with online awards, national competitions in front of expert juries (January–May), and the in-person festival in Luxembourg on 6-9 July 2027, where national champions exhibit, pitch on stage and compete for European awards such as the JA Europe Company of the Year.

Participation is through the national JA organisation in your country (JA operates in 40+ European countries, including Georgia through JA Georgia). Teams usually pay no fee; national winners are supported to attend the festival.
highlights: Run a real student company and compete for Company of the Year
National champions travel to Luxembourg, 6-9 July 2027
ja-europe-gen-e-2027-luxembourg.eligibility: Students aged roughly 15-24 taking part in a JA Company Programme or Start Up Programme through their national JA organisation in Europe.
how_to_apply: Contact your national JA organisation or ask your school about the JA Company Programme.
Form a team and run your mini-company during the 2026-27 school year.
Join Virtual Gen-E and enter your national competition (January–May 2027).
If you win nationally, represent your country at Gen-E in Luxembourg.
ja-europe-gen-e-2027-luxembourg.costs: Usually free for students; costs of national finalists attending the festival are normally arranged through national JA organisations.

ja-europe-ups-healthcare-award-2027.about:
The UPS Healthcare Award, run by JA Europe with UPS Healthcare, celebrates youth-led innovation in healthcare and healthcare logistics. It is open to JA alumni aged 18-30 who are founders or co-founders of a healthcare start-up.

The first round closes on 31 December 2026; top start-ups are announced by 30 January 2027 and interviewed in February/March 2027. The three winners gain visibility, mentoring and networking with senior UPS Healthcare leaders.

It is a good fit for alumni of the JA Company Programme or Start Up Programme who have moved on to build a health-tech or logistics venture.
highlights: Open to JA alumni founders aged 18-30
Focus on healthcare and healthcare-logistics innovation
Visibility and networking with UPS Healthcare leadership
ja-europe-ups-healthcare-award-2027.eligibility: JA alumni aged 18-30 who are founders or co-founders of a start-up in the healthcare industry.

Prepare a description of your start-up and its healthcare solution.
Apply via the link on the JA Europe page by 31 December 2026.
Interview in February/March 2027 if shortlisted.

jugend-forscht-2027.about:
Jugend forscht invites young people to pick their own research question in seven fields (working world, biology, chemistry, earth and space sciences, mathematics/informatics, physics, technology) and present it at a regional contest, then the state and national rounds. There are two age groups: 'Schüler experimentieren' (Jugend forscht junior, 4th grade to 14) and Jugend forscht (15–21).

You register online by 30 November 2026, then submit a written report in January and present at a regional contest in February/March 2027. National winners can represent Germany at the EU Contest for Young Scientists and other international fairs.

The competition is in German and aimed at students living or studying in Germany (including German schools abroad).
highlights: Path to national final and EUCYS
Individual or teams of up to three
jugend-forscht-2027.eligibility: Young people from 4th grade up to age 21 who attend school, an apprenticeship or university in Germany, or a German school abroad; individuals or teams of up to three. German-language project work.

Register online by 30 November 2026
Write up your project (written work due in January)
Present at your regional contest in Feb/Mar 2027
jugend-forscht-2027.costs: Free to enter; regional, state and national contests are free for participants.

jugend-innovativ-2027.about:
Jugend Innovativ, run by the federal promotional bank aws for the Austrian ministries, is the country's main youth innovation contest and Austria's route to international events such as EUCYS and ISEF. Students submit a project idea in one of six categories (Design & Creation, Engineering, Entrepreneurship, ICT & Digital, Science, Sustainability), develop it over the school year with coaching, and the best teams present at the national final.

Winners receive cash prizes and bonuses and can be nominated for international competitions and events.
highlights: Six categories from design to science
jugend-innovativ-2027.eligibility: Pupils, apprentices and people in their first year of vocational training aged 15–20, at schools/companies in Austria; individuals or teams. Projects in German.

Develop the project with your teacher during the year
Present at the regional/national final if selected

KEDGE's International Winter School in Paris offers two intensive one-week modules on technology, management and innovation (each 24 contact hours, formally assessed, 5 ECTS), a business visit or talk per course, a guided tour of Paris, a welcome event and a dinner. Students can take one week (5 ECTS) or both (10 ECTS) and receive official transcripts and a certificate.

It is aimed at motivated advanced bachelor's and master's students with at least B2 English. The intake starts on 11 January 2027; places are limited and allocated first-come, first-served.

kenyon-review-patricia-grodd-poetry-priz.about:
The Patricia Grodd Poetry Prize is one of the best-known youth poetry awards in the US literary world. Students submit poems online during November; the winner and two runners-up are published in The Kenyon Review, a leading literary magazine.

The winner receives a full scholarship to a Kenyon Review Young Writers summer workshop (or an online workshop for past residential attendees). There is no entry fee and no stated country restriction.

Submit via kenyonreview.org/submit/patricia-grodd/ between 1 and 30 November
